name: Cove Pendant
imageAlt: Pale concrete pendant lamp hanging against a teal wall
description: A soft concrete shade with a bright interior. It looks heavy and hangs like it isn't. Use it over a table or in a hallway where one lamp is enough.
dimensions: Shade Ø 32 cm, drop up to 150 cm

name: Loft Pendant
imageAlt: White enamel pendant lamp above a concrete dining table
description: A wide enamel shade that throws light down and leaves the rest of the room quiet. Hung over a table, it does the job of a dining lamp without the ceremony.
dimensions: Shade Ø 36 cm, drop up to 160 cm

name: Hale Floor Lamp
imageAlt: Charcoal adjustable floor lamp against a white wall
description: A working lamp with a heavy lean. The shade tilts and stays put, which is the whole point of a lamp you actually read under.

name: Dome Cluster
imageAlt: Five brushed-brass dome pendants hanging at different heights
description: Five brushed-brass domes, meant to hang at uneven heights. Sold as a set, so the composition arrives together.

name: Arc Floor Lamp
imageAlt: Brushed steel arc floor lamp reaching over a round table
description: A steel arc that reaches across a seating group. The shade stays out of the conversation and the light lands where people sit.

name: Grove Sofa
imageAlt: Deep green velvet sofa with oak legs
description: Deep green velvet, two loose backs, and short oak legs. A sofa with a low line that does not try to be a cloud.

name: Button Lounge
imageAlt: Ivory button-tufted lounge chair with turned legs
description: Ivory linen, a tight buttoned back, and turned legs. A small chair that takes a corner without looking temporary.

name: Ridge Chair
imageAlt: Grey wool dining chair with oak legs
description: A dining chair with a tall wool back and oak legs. Firm enough for a long meal, light enough to pull in.

name: Slot Stool
imageAlt: Pale ash stool with a slot cut into the seat
description: An ash stool with a handhold cut into the seat. Light enough to move, solid enough to stand on.

name: Cafe Table
imageAlt: Round white cafe table with oak legs
description: A round white top on splayed oak legs. The chairs in the photograph are for scale — the table is sold on its own.

name: Drawer Console
imageAlt: Oak console table with three drawers and round pulls
description: Three oak drawers, round pulls, and a thin steel frame. It holds the things that otherwise land on the dining table.

name: Tripod Side Table
imageAlt: Small white side table with three tapered wooden legs
description: A small round top on three tapered legs. Built for a lamp, a glass, and not much else.

name: Archive Rug
imageAlt: Sand and gold patterned rug, partly rolled, with fringe
description: A sand ground with a dense border and fringe. More formal than the rest of the edit, which is why it works under a plain table.

name: Field Throw
imageAlt: Charcoal grid wool throw draped on a brown sofa
description: A charcoal wool throw with a thin ochre grid. It is the layer that makes a sofa look finished. The sofa in the photograph is not included.

name: Day Cushion
imageAlt: Firm white cotton cushion on a white plinth
description: A firm cushion in washed cotton. Simple enough to stack, shaped enough to stay put. The yellow in the photograph is the backdrop.

name: Tide Side Plates
imageAlt: Stack of pale blue stoneware plates on a wooden shelf
description: A set of four stoneware plates with a pale blue pool in the middle and a toasted rim. Each one sits a little differently, on purpose.

name: Kiln Cup Set
imageAlt: Speckled ceramic beaker and smaller cups on a white shelf
description: A speckled beaker and four smaller cups, glazed in the same firing. Use them for coffee or leave them on the shelf.

name: Speck Bottle Vases
imageAlt: Three pale speckled ceramic bottle vases
description: Three bottle vases in a pale speckled glaze. The heights are staggered so they read as a group.

name: Offset Shelf
imageAlt: Modular oak wall shelves with closed boxes and an open rail
description: A modular oak wall shelf with closed boxes and an open rail. Arrange the blocks once, then leave them alone. The objects in the photograph are styling.
